A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CTNN research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on physics prediction, graph and complex classification, and additional vision, sequence, regression and text tasks in its appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a mixed-boundary anisotropic diffusion experiment on simplicial complexes in Appendix H.5.

M1.justification: v3 adds a residual transport-diffusion specialization with a step-size rule in Appendix C.1 and boundary-aware PDE training using Dirichlet clamping and Robin residuals in H.5. The general CTNN message-passing rules, transformer pseudocode and map catalogue remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix H.5 adds reaction–anisotropic diffusion on irregular triangulations with holes and mixed Dirichlet–Robin boundary conditions. This extends the earlier grid-based PDE evaluations to a distinct geometric and boundary-condition scenario; previous task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v3 adds an evaluated Cellular Transformer baseline attributed to Barsbey et al. (2025) in Table 17. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new H.5 experiment introduces finite-element reference solutions, vertex-level regression, boundary enforcement and a comparison matched in depth, width and attention heads. Reported splits, metrics and training budgets for the retained experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 11 adds qualitative comparisons of predicted fields and boundary behavior across several perforated mesh geometries. Existing polygon-complexity and attention-capacity analyses are retained; H.1's mechanistic discussion does not report a new measured ablation.

E5.justification: Repeated-run counts and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged for retained experiments. The new four-seed PDE comparison follows the existing reporting practice, without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests or a revised uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: Matched existing results are unchanged apart from equivalent numerical formatting. New Table 17 reports test MSE of 0.3277 ± 0.0408 for Cellular Transformer and 0.3172 ± 0.0365 for Copresheaf Cellular Transformer; Figure 11 adds corresponding qualitative predictions.

T1.justification: v3 adds copresheaf Laplacian and energy definitions, positivity/kernel and energy-decay theorems, a strict SNN-containment theorem, and computational-complexity derivations. The earlier approximation and sheaf-representation proofs remain. The new diffusion argument contains an inconsistency between Equation 11 and Theorem 2 for general transport maps.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: CTNNs unify existing architectures through directional, heterogeneous transport and improve structured-data learning. Stronger wording and additional supporting material do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving upwind-like transport, phase preservation and diffusion geometry, and attributes gains to geometric structure independently of parameter count. It also interprets the new PDE predictions as improving boundary recovery. The stated overhead and modest-scale limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: H.5 documents finite-element target generation, vertex/edge features, map initialization, normalization, AdamW scheduling and gradient clipping at 0.8. v3 also clarifies the MUTAG CopresheafGCN map dimension as D=7. No new code or data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds explicit connections to quiver Laplacians and cellular transformers, citing Sumray et al. (2024), Ballester et al. (2024) and Barsbey et al. (2025). It also revises several higher-order-learning references while retaining the broad unifying research position; duplicate-reference consolidation is editorial.

P1.justification: v3 copyedits the main text, promotes Related Work to a numbered section, relabels several constructions as definitions, and expands worked explanations and cross-references. The main narrative and most existing appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands visual exposition with an architecture overview table, an edge-adjacency example, sheaf-message and cross-attention diagrams, PDE comparison panels and a complexity table. It also redraws the incidence example. Existing empirical displays are mostly retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful explanatory diagrams and a relevant mesh-PDE comparison while retaining v1's results. However, Appendix C's incoming-message expression does not reproduce the outgoing-adjoint terms in Theorem 2 for general transports, undermining the new CTNN energy-decay guarantee. The gains in coverage and clarity coexist with a substantive new correctness problem, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
